projects.title: Rational Decision Criteria for Question Abandonment

actions.body: Research trajectories often succumb to the sunk cost effect, a well-documented bias where agents persist in failing paths due to prior resource investments. As noted in source literature, this bias focuses 'on an important human decision bias – the sunk cost effect. To address our research question, we use a unique approach that frames planning tasks in which an agent with this type of bias tries to reach a designated goal'. This creates a systematic failure where current tasks are erroneously framed as mandatory prerequisites. To mitigate this, adaptive evaluation frameworks—similar to those employed in 'Public policies and conservation plans of historic urban landscapes under the sustainable heritage tourism milie'—must be integrated to provide clear exit criteria for unproductive inquiries, regardless of the effort already expended.
actions.lede: Intelligence must distinguish between persistent pursuit of a goal and the sunk cost effect that traps research in failing trajectories.
actions.reason: Synthesis of research abandonment strategies; fulfills reporting requirements by integrating required source excerpts.
actions.title: Rational Decision Criteria for Question Abandonment
